nodes.html: What happens when a return is overdue
nodes.text: What happens when a return is overdue

nodes.html: The ATO may apply a failure-to-lodge (FTL) penalty when a required tax return or statement is not lodged by the due date. The amount can depend on how late the lodgment is and the size of the entity. If lodging results in tax being payable and the amount is overdue, general interest charge (GIC) may apply to the outstanding debt. For businesses, unresolved tax and super obligations can lead to stronger ATO recovery action in some circumstances, including garnishee notices and, for certain company liabilities, director penalty notices. If overdue lodgments remain unresolved, the ATO can issue a default assessment using the information available to it. Acting early minimises the damage.

nodes.html: A registered tax agent can lodge overdue returns, request remission of FTL penalties where there are mitigating circumstances, negotiate payment plans for any debt, and communicate with the ATO on your behalf. Agents often have extended lodgement deadlines, which can buy time. The key is to engage before the ATO escalates to enforcement.

nodes.html: If you are several years behind, the matched agent works through the backlog methodically — reconstructing income where records are missing, reconciling bank data, and lodging each year in sequence. The ATO generally prefers voluntary catch-up over enforcement, so engaging an agent is almost always better than continuing to delay. Tell us how many years you are behind in the questionnaire.

nodes.q: What happens if I don't lodge my tax return?
nodes.a: The ATO may apply a failure-to-lodge (FTL) penalty when a return is not lodged by the due date, and general interest charge (GIC) may apply to any overdue tax debt. If overdue lodgments remain unresolved, the ATO can issue a default assessment using the information available to it. For businesses, unresolved tax and super obligations can lead to stronger recovery action, including garnishee notices and, for certain company liabilities, director penalty notices. Engaging a registered agent early minimises the damage.
nodes.aText: The ATO may apply a failure-to-lodge (FTL) penalty when a return is not lodged by the due date, and general interest charge (GIC) may apply to any overdue tax debt. If overdue lodgments remain unresolved, the ATO can issue a default assessment using the information available to it. For businesses, unresolved tax and super obligations can lead to stronger recovery action, including garnishee notices and, for certain company liabilities, director penalty notices. Engaging a registered agent early minimises the damage.

nodes.q: Can I lodge multiple overdue tax returns at once?
nodes.a: Yes. The matched agent works through the backlog year by year, reconstructing income where records are missing and lodging each return in sequence. The ATO generally prefers voluntary catch-up over enforcement, so engaging an agent is far better than continuing to delay.
nodes.aText: Yes. The matched agent works through the backlog year by year, reconstructing income where records are missing and lodging each return in sequence. The ATO generally prefers voluntary catch-up over enforcement, so engaging an agent is far better than continuing to delay.

nodes.q: Can penalties be reduced or waived?
nodes.a: Potentially. A registered agent can request remission of failure-to-lodge penalties where mitigating circumstances exist (illness, disaster, family crisis). Remission is not guaranteed, but a well-prepared request improves the chances. The matched agent assesses your situation.

nodes.q: What if I owe tax I can't pay?
nodes.a: If you cannot pay an assessed tax debt in full, you may be eligible for an ATO payment plan. A registered tax agent can help you understand your options and deal with the ATO on your behalf. GIC generally continues to accrue on the outstanding balance during a payment arrangement.
nodes.aText: If you cannot pay an assessed tax debt in full, you may be eligible for an ATO payment plan. A registered tax agent can help you understand your options and deal with the ATO on your behalf. GIC generally continues to accrue on the outstanding balance during a payment arrangement.

nodes.q: How do I know if I'm several years behind?
nodes.a: Check myGov for individual returns, or your accounting software for business lodgements. If you are unsure which years are outstanding, tell us in the questionnaire and the matched agent will confirm your lodgement status with the ATO before preparing any catch-up returns.
nodes.aText: Check myGov for individual returns, or your accounting software for business lodgements. If you are unsure which years are outstanding, tell us in the questionnaire and the matched agent will confirm your lodgement status with the ATO before preparing any catch-up returns.

nodes.q: Will the ATO know I've come forward voluntarily?
nodes.a: Yes — and voluntary catch-up is viewed far more favourably than waiting for the ATO to chase you. Engaging a registered agent to lodge overdue returns signals good faith and often leads to better outcomes on penalty remission and payment-plan terms.
nodes.aText: Yes — and voluntary catch-up is viewed far more favourably than waiting for the ATO to chase you. Engaging a registered agent to lodge overdue returns signals good faith and often leads to better outcomes on penalty remission and payment-plan terms.

nodes.q: How quickly can a registered agent start on my overdue returns?
nodes.a: Most matches are completed within 60 seconds of finishing the questionnaire. Your matched firm will typically reach out within 2 hours to review your situation and begin the catch-up process, or you can call for immediate assistance.
nodes.aText: Most matches are completed within 60 seconds of finishing the questionnaire. Your matched firm will typically reach out within 2 hours to review your situation and begin the catch-up process, or you can call for immediate assistance.

nodes.q: Can overdue returns affect my credit or business loans?
nodes.a: Unresolved tax debts can lead to ATO recovery action that appears on credit reports, and outstanding director penalty notices can affect personal credit. Lodging overdue returns and arranging payment plans proactively with a registered agent helps protect your credit position.
